records.title: Approaching the Human Cognitive Domain
records.summary: Research synthesis examining emerging pathways for AI systems to infer, model, predict, influence, monitor, and partially externalise aspects of human cognitive state, and the resulting need for a dedicated human cognitive integrity governance domain.
records.research_method: Structured synthesis of peer-reviewed research, official programmes, legislation, policy, and governance analysis.
records.research_scope: Neural decoding, neuroprostheses, passive cognitive proxies, digital phenotyping, human digital twins, persuasive AI, quantum biosensing, defence programmes and international neurotechnology governance. Unsupported telepathy and generic remote mind-reading claims are expressly excluded.
records.governance_purpose: Provide the research basis for PROP-0001 and the subsequent creation of the MENTIS domain instruments recorded by PATCH-0023.
records.limitations: The synthesis spans heterogeneous fields with different evidence standards; many capabilities are laboratory- or clinical-context dependent; some future timelines are judgmental; and the original research thread remains supplementary rather than a substitute for the recovered public bibliography.

records.title: Deception and Unscrupulous Conduct in Frontier AI Development
records.summary: Research synthesis supporting a strong policy presumption against deliberately optimising, selecting, retaining, or recursively cultivating AI systems for deception, manipulation, concealment, monitor evasion, sabotage, policy laundering, or related unscrupulous conduct, including where the stated purpose is defensive evaluation.
records.research_method: Structured synthesis of academic research, frontier-model system cards, laboratory safety publications, government policy, legislation, standards guidance, and reported incidents.
records.research_scope: Empirical evidence concerning deception, alignment faking, emergent misalignment, reward hacking, monitor evasion and sabotage; system-card and incident evidence; and law or policy relevant to deliberately cultivating deceptive capability. Ordinary model error without strategic selection is outside the central prohibition.
records.governance_purpose: Provide the evidence basis for FM-0047 and PROP-0019, distinguishing legitimate elicitation and measurement from prohibited cultivation of deceptive capability.
records.limitations: Controlled evaluations may not predict production prevalence; system cards are provider-authored; the July 2026 incident record lacks full internal telemetry; legal sources regulate different conduct and jurisdictions; and the proposed prohibition is a governance synthesis rather than a statement of existing universal law.

records.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons and Long-Horizon Agent Governance
records.summary: Multi-source research synthesis of METR's task-completion time-horizon programme, benchmark construction, revisions, domain limits, evaluation-integrity findings and implications for governing sustained agent trajectories.
records.research_method: Direct review of METR's current metric page, original paper, TH1.1 revision, cross-domain analysis, HCAST and RE-Bench materials, Frontier Risk Report and public model-evaluation reports. Claims are separated into measurement findings, extrapolations, limitations and VIGIL governance inferences.
records.research_scope: Task-completion time horizons as a measure of agent capability; benchmark composition and revision; reliability thresholds; domain and scaffold sensitivity; benchmark integrity; relationship to long-horizon governance. The record does not assess consciousness, general intelligence, or a universal duration of autonomous operation.
records.governance_purpose: Provide an evidence basis for long-horizon persistence, optimiser-trajectory, authority-continuity, monitoring-capability and evaluation-integrity governance without treating a benchmark horizon as proof of general autonomy or harmful intent.
records.limitations: The reviewed task suites remain concentrated in self-contained software, ML and cybersecurity work; public and internal-frontier estimates are scaffold-, access- and task-distribution-dependent; measurements above the suite's supported range are unreliable; and some model-level evidence is disclosed only in aggregated form.

records.title: Expenditure Horizons, Test-Time Scaling and Parallel Agentic Optimisation
records.summary: Research synthesis of METR's expenditure-horizon proposal, NanoGPT experiment, agent-ability metric taxonomy, RE-Bench evidence and related test-time scaling results, with bounded implications for aggregate-pathway governance.
records.research_method: Comparative review of METR's expenditure-horizon experiment and metrics note against RE-Bench, time-horizon methodology, test-time scaling literature and model-system-card reporting. The review separates measured NanoGPT results from broader governance inferences about budget, parallelism and repeated search.
records.research_scope: Agent optimisation performance as a function of expenditure; common-unit comparison with human effort; within-trajectory and between-trajectory scaling; parallel experiment execution; repeated attempts; validation and mergeability; implications for cumulative trajectory controls. The record does not estimate economy-wide AI R&D acceleration.
records.governance_purpose: Distinguish serial task horizon from budget-scaled and parallel optimisation, and provide an evidence basis for aggregate-pathway controls where many cheap actions or attempts can search broadly for a successful route.
records.limitations: The NanoGPT application is one highly instrumented, cheap-to-score optimisation problem; human-effort estimates are uncertain; expenditure depends on prices and included costs; agent contributions require revalidation and mergeability review; and the metric can be unstable or undefined under some curve shapes.

records.title: Monitorability, Covert Side Tasks and Consequential Intervention
records.summary: Research synthesis of METR's SHUSHCAST programme, QA monitor-evasion studies, chain-of-thought findings, Frontier Risk Report, agent incidents and model evaluations, separating coverage, capability, integrity, classification and intervention.
records.research_method: Direct comparison of METR's monitorability experiments, precursor QA studies, multi-laboratory Frontier Risk Report, agent-incident dataset and model-evaluation reports, with external primary research on chain-of-thought monitorability and unfaithfulness used to test alternative interpretations.
records.research_scope: AI monitors for agent actions and reasoning; covert side-task evaluation; reasoning visibility; relative monitor capability; monitor coverage and bypass; human and agent elicitation; production-monitoring claims; and the downstream gap between detection and consequential intervention.
records.governance_purpose: Distinguish monitor capability, monitor coverage, monitor bypass, detection quality, escalation and intervention so monitoring is not treated as one binary safeguard or as proof that detected conduct was contained.
records.limitations: METR characterises the core SHUSHCAST results as early-stage; task sets are small; elicitation is incomplete; access to reasoning differs across providers; some findings concern human red-team bypasses rather than autonomous agent execution; and private monitoring configurations and raw production alert records are unavailable.

records.title: Conflict-condition threat signals, defensive interception and offensive-authority renewal: external evidence review
records.summary: A bounded review of public evidence concerning defensive interception, renewed hostile activity and offensive operations, military AI/data-assisted intelligence, humanitarian ground truth, and neutral intermediaries. The factual substrate is corroborated, but no reviewed source establishes automated offensive reauthorisation; the ‘perpetual war token’ remains a low-confidence governance inference and analytical metaphor only.
records.evidence_confidence: corroborated factual substrate; unverified low-confidence authority-coupling inference
records.research_method: Direct review of official, wire-service, and major-news sources supplied in the originating handoff, with claim-level separation between observed facts, contested accounts, counter-evidence, and governance inference. Sources were selected to preserve defensive-system function, conflict sequence, AI/data-system relevance, humanitarian evidence, and neutral-intermediary roles without inferring a shared technical architecture.
records.research_scope: Public reporting and official material concerning Israel and Gaza from October 2023 through June 2025. The review excludes classified systems, undisclosed command workflows, source-code architecture, and any claim that a literal or functional perpetual-war token was deployed.
records.governance_purpose: To support classification of two organisation-neutral VIGIL failure modes and a narrow Caelestis authority-separation proposal while preventing a contested real-world narrative from being converted into asserted fact or CAM doctrine.
records.limitations: Public sources do not expose complete targeting, command-authorisation, interception-control, or software-architecture records. Reuters material was reviewed through a syndication copy. No source establishes integration between defensive interception and offensive targeting controls, causal automation between a hostile event and renewed offensive authority, or the provenance of any alleged authority token.
